intro.variant: 亻 on the left edge (ninben). 𠆢 as a roof on top: 今, 会, 合.
intro.clue: A pair of legs mid-stride, seen from the side. Everything human in kanji hangs off this shape.
s2: Same two strokes, opposite crossing. 人 has the long stroke on the left; 入 tucks it under the right.
A person who has stopped walking and thrown both arms wide.
The legs split apart and never meet. No head, no join.
s2x: The 大 sub-family
Add one line to 大 and you get more kanji: 天 heaven (a lid above the person), 太 fat (a belly-dot underneath), 犬 dog (a dot by the ear), and at N3 夫 husband (a pin through the hair).
s3: A person props themselves against a tree trunk and stops walking.
A person's origin, the thing they were issued at birth, is the body.
A person plus motion. Japan invented this one: moving people are working people.
intro.footer: 人 is the highest-frequency human element in the language. Learn 亻 and roughly one N4 kanji in eight opens up.

intro.variant: Small and inside a character: mouth. Large and wrapping the whole character (囗): an enclosure, not a mouth.
intro.clue: An open mouth drawn square. If a kanji involves speaking, eating, naming or a hole, look for it.
s2: 口 with one bar through the middle. This is the single most useful distinction on the page.
口 with two bars: a pupil and an iris stacked inside.
口 with a full cross inside: paddies divided by paths.
s2x: Mouth or box?
国 country and 図 diagram use the big enclosure 囗. 品 and 味 use the small mouth. Same square, different job: check the size before you file it.
s3: Something your mouth has not yet finished deciding about: its taste.
Three mouths all talking about the same thing: that is how goods get a reputation.
The mouth stretched out to reach someone at a distance.
intro.footer: 口 is a component in over thirty N5 and N4 kanji. Its only real difficulty is telling it from 日, 目 and 田.

intro.variant: Same shape wherever it sits: left (時), top (早), bottom (春), inside (間).
intro.clue: A circle with a dot at the centre, squared off by the brush. Sun by picture, day by consequence.
s2: One extra bar inside. 目 is taller than it is wide; 日 is squarer.
日 with a drop of light on top: the sun just breaking, bleaching everything.
日 with a vertical added, so the bar becomes a full cross.
s2x: Time lives here
日 marks the passage of time in 時 hour, 曜 weekday, 早 early, 昼 noon, 間 interval. If a kanji is about when, check for the sun.
s3: Sun and moon in the sky at once: the brightest thing you can draw.
The temple bell and the sun together are how a day gets divided into hours.
No sun, only sound. When you can hear but not see, it is dark.
intro.footer: Sun on the left almost always means time. Sun elsewhere usually means light or heat.

intro.variant: Squeezed narrow on the left (校, 村). Doubled and tripled for scale: 林, 森.
intro.clue: A trunk, two branches, two roots. One of the cleanest pictographs in the set.
s2: A mark cut across the roots, pointing at where the tree comes from. Hence origin, hence the thing that holds knowledge.
The mark moves to the top and grows long. The far tip of the branches: the end.
Same as 末 but the top bar is short: the tree has not finished growing up there yet.
s2x: 末 or 未?
Top stroke longer than the one below it: 末, the end. Top stroke shorter: 未, not yet. A genuine exam trap and worth ten seconds now.
s3: Two trees standing next to each other. You can still walk between them.
Land measured out around a tree: the shade where people settled.
Wooden benches where people cross paths and mingle. That is a school.
intro.footer: 木 with a mark on it is a small-change kanji. 木 next to something else is a compound. Sort each one that way as you meet it.

intro.variant: 氵 three drops on the left: by far the commonest form.
intro.clue: A current with spray flying off both banks. On the left it collapses to three splashes.
s2: 水 with a single frozen droplet stuck to its side.
水 with a drop added on top: a stream so long it never ends.
永 with an extra flick. Reaching for water is the oldest kind of seeking.
s2x: Three drops, one meaning
氵 never means anything but water or liquid. Spot it and you already have half the meaning: 海 sea, 池 pond, 洗 wash, 洋 ocean.
s3: Water first, before anything else happens. Wash your hands before you eat.
Water that goes on forever: you had better know how to swim.
Water aimed at the main spot. Pour it there, and put your attention there too.
intro.footer: 氵 is the single most productive left-hand element in the kanji you'll meet next. Learn it once, use it forty times.

intro.variant: 扌 on the left (tehen): the hand turned sideways to grab.
intro.clue: Four fingers and a wrist, drawn as three horizontals down one vertical.
s2: Same skeleton, but the bottom stroke curls up instead of hooking down. Hand grips, hair curls.
Two horizontals, not three, and no hook at all.
Like 午 but the top stroke lifts: a horn poking up.
s2x: Hook or no hook
手 and 毛 both hook; 午 and 牛 do not. Write the hook deliberately and these four stop blurring together.
s3: Carrying something to the temple, in your hands, all the way there.
A hand flat against armour plating. You are not lifting it, you are pushing.
The part of the hand that carries your meaning: you point with it.
intro.footer: 扌 always means a deliberate physical action done by a person. At N5 and N4 you only meet it in 持, but N3 brings a flood: 押 push, 指 finger, 投 throw, 打 hit.

intro.variant: 忄 upright on the left (risshinben). 心 sits underneath at the bottom.
intro.clue: A heart with three drops flying off it. In Japanese it covers the mind as well as the emotions.
s2: 心 with a stroke driven straight through it. What goes through your heart, you must do.
The same heart stood upright and squeezed thin: 忙 busy, 快 pleasant, 情 feeling.
Four dots at the bottom, easily mistaken for a heart. 黒 black and 無 nothing use fire, not heart.
s2x: Where the heart sits
Bottom position means the feeling is the result: 思 think, 急 hurry, 悪 bad. Left position means the feeling is the manner: 忙 busy.
s3: A heart with a field laid over it: mind divided into neat plots. That is thinking.
The sound your heart makes before you say it out loud.
A second-rate heart. Not broken, just not good.
intro.footer: 心 at the bottom is a feeling you arrive at. 忄 on the left is a feeling you are already in.

intro.variant: Unchanged on the left in Japanese (Chinese shrinks it to 讠, Japanese does not).
intro.clue: A mouth at the bottom with sound waves stacked above it, and a lid on top.
s2: Almost identical, but 音 has 日 at the base where 言 has 口. Sound comes out of the sun, words out of the mouth.
The top half of 言 on its own: a figure planted on the ground.
What sits inside 話. A mouth with something sticking out of it.
s2x: 言 or 音?
Bottom box has a bar through it (日): 音, sound. Bottom box is empty (口): 言, words. Nothing else distinguishes them.
s3: Words plus tongue. Speaking is words that have actually left the body.
The words I claim as mine: my language.
Words put up for sale. Somebody has to buy them and read them.
intro.footer: 言 on the left is close to a guarantee that the kanji involves language. It is the most reliable predictor in this deck.

intro.variant: Narrowed on the left, with the bottom three dots compressed (紙, 終).
intro.clue: A skein of silk hanging from a hook, with loose ends at the bottom.
s2: Same lower half, but the top is a cross, not a coil. Grain scattered rather than thread wound.
糸 with a stroke added on top: threads traced back to a single source.
糸 under a lid. Thread before anything is done to it: raw material.
s2x: Thread means continuity
Anything long, joined or ongoing tends to take 糸. At N3 you'll meet 続 continue, 線 line and 結 tie.
s3: Fibres pressed flat so a family can write its name on them.
The thread runs out in winter. Nothing comes after.
Coloured threads meeting on a cloth: the oldest kind of picture.
intro.footer: 糸 on the left is quiet but consistent: connection, duration, or something woven.

intro.variant: Always full-size, always wrapping whatever goes inside it.
intro.clue: A pair of saloon doors facing each other. Whatever you put between them is the story.
s2: Put the sun 日 in the gateway. The gap of daylight between the doors is the interval.
Two hands 开 lifting the bar out of the doorway.
才 wedged across the gap, jamming the doors shut.
s2x: Why this family is easy
門 kanji are the most learnable set there is. There is exactly one variable, what is inside, and the answer always drives the meaning.
s3: An ear pressed to the gate, listening for what is on the other side.
A mouth at the gate. You cannot come in until you have answered.
The bolt in the gate: what connects the two halves, and what stops you.
intro.footer: Learn 門 once and the rest of the family comes almost free. Highest return of any shape in Tier 1.

intro.variant: 辶 (shinnyō) always sweeps in from the left and runs underneath the rest of the kanji.
intro.clue: A footprint with a road unrolling beneath it: a foot and a path fused into one stroke set.
s2: 辶 plus 入 enter. Everyone moving in at once. Made in Japan, no Chinese original.
辶 plus 刀 sword. As far as you can walk before someone stops you.
辶 plus 反 reverse. Movement in the reverse direction: give it back.
s2x: Direction is the whole point
Every 辶 kanji is movement plus a direction: 進 forward, 返 back, 近 near, 遠 far, 送 away from you.
s3: Your head pointed down a path. The way you are heading is your way.
Movement through a funnel: in one end, out the other.
One full lap of the road. Seven days and you are back where you started.
intro.footer: 辶 is written last, sweeping under everything else. Write it first and the balance never recovers.

intro.variant: Same shape on the right (動) or at the bottom (男, 勉).
intro.clue: A flexed arm, or a plough being driven into the ground. Two strokes, enormous mileage.
s2: The hook sits at the top right instead of the top left. 力 pushes, 刀 cuts.
One extra horizontal across the top.
The second stroke crosses the first instead of tucking under it.
s2x: Two strokes, four kanji
力 刀 万 九 differ only by where a stroke starts and whether it crosses. Write all four side by side once and the confusion stops.
s3: Strength applied to a field. This is the historical picture, not a modern claim.
Force applied to something heavy. Motion is what happens next.
Effort spent escaping ignorance. Which is what you are doing right now.
intro.footer: 力 almost always sits last in the writing order and last in the story: it is the effort applied to whatever came before.
